Post-mortem tenderisation is influenced by enzymatic degradation of myofibrillar and associated cytoskeletal proteins. These proteins function to maintain myofibrillar integrity and it is known that the calpain system, in parti- cular calpain 1, is responsible for proteolysis of these pro- teins [10,12,13,15]. The calpain family of Ca2+-dependent proteases are thus key proteins in the regulation of tender- ness [58-60].
